rows.evidence: Line 202 is inside validateRunSnapshot itself, the RunSnapshot@1 validator registered at record-readers.ts:341-344; the store applies it to every unbound record before commit (record-codec.ts:634-639 via applyRecordSchema :369-397). The only writer of an executionHistory is the Run machine (run-machine.ts:870-871, :991), and a write goes through locatorAfter, which rebuilds the locator and rejects a bad shape at :1242-1244 (locatorShapeOk at :1212-1221 rejects observedThroughPosition 0) and takes its sessionRef from the claim (claim-service.ts:997 refuses another project). A search for `executionHistory:` in src finds only those two Run-machine sites. A malformed stored locator therefore needs a hand-edited/old/shadow-written row; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Keeping the commit/read validator boundary without a tamper test is right (AGENTS rule 4); no deletion is coherent here because the validator is the codec that rejects the damaged row.

rows.evidence: Line 785 is the schemaId check of validateRecord (:784-797), the body of the registered CoreOperation/Session/SessionWorkLink validators (SESSION_RECORD_SCHEMAS :882-909) and of the typed decoders (:1012-1035). The store selects the schema from the record's own schemaId (record-codec.ts:558) and checks aggregateType from that body (:565-571), and every writer encodes a link with SESSION_WORK_LINK_SCHEMA_ID (:994; claim-service.ts:1263, session-lifecycle.ts:417, session-responsibility-service.ts:176-180). Every decodeSessionWorkLink call site passes a record read by that work-link ref key (session-links.ts:54, claim-service.ts:1004, session-lifecycle.ts:363, session-responsibility-service.ts:112). A record carrying another schemaId under a work-link ref key can only be a hand-edited/foreign row; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Keeping it untested is right (rule 4); there is no production writer of a mismatched schemaId, so no test can reach it without tampering.

rows.evidence: Line 1032 returns a failed decodeSessionWorkLink. The strict payload rule at :1030-1031 is checkWorkLinkBody(body, true), which requires a bound `since` cursor (:765-770). Every writer that creates a link registers a commit-cursor binding for `since` (session-directory.ts:1008-1013, session-lifecycle.ts:390-395 and :422, session-responsibility-service.ts:176-181, claim-service.ts:1263-1279), and a closing link keeps the stored `since` (session-lifecycle.ts:393, session-responsibility-service.ts:176-180); the store re-validates the bound record with this same strict validator (record-codec.ts:604-640). So a link with a null/unbound `since` cannot be committed, and only a damaged/foreign row reaches the arm. U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Keeping the read-side rejection untested is right; deleting it would turn a damaged link into an accepted unbound interval.

rows.evidence: Line 661 rejects an operation action with no provenance. The only current-format creator is admitSessionCreation: it fills {schemaVersion:1, kind:'new'} when the key is omitted or a validated value when present (session-directory.ts:704-712), and writes it into action.provenance (:782). The completed operation spreads the stored one (:968-982), so replay also keeps it. SessionOperationRecord requires it (session-contracts.ts:27-28), and the record validator runs on commit (record-codec.ts:634-639). Only a pre-slice-1 or hand-edited operation lacks it; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Keep it and do not add a tamper test (rule 4): it is the current-format requirement T introduced with the provenance backfill removal, and no production writer omits the field.

rows.evidence: Line 664 reports checkSessionProvenance(actionProvenance, ref.projectId, planned.sessionId) failing. On the write path the same pure check already ran with the same ids before any commit: session-directory.ts:710-712 uses scope.projectId and the derived sessionId, and the record's ref.projectId/plannedSessionRef.sessionId are set from that same scope at :694 and :772. checkSessionProvenance (session-record-codecs.ts:381-430) is pure and depends only on those ids, so a writer that accepted the value cannot produce a record failing this line; the commit validator (record-codec.ts:634-639) therefore never fires here. Only a hand-edited or old-format operation with a bad provenance value reaches it; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Keeping it untested is right (rule 4); no other validator or writer depends on removing it.

rows.evidence: Line 345 counts an activity record whose stored sessionRef is null. A null is written only by run-activity-service.ts:288-309, at :302, when the Run has no DispatchOutboxEntry. Every Run is created by the claim effect pair create_run+create_outbox (state/task-machine.ts:925-932; claim-service.ts:456-466, :480-482) in one commit, and the store has no production record deletion, so a current Run always has its outbox. End commits pass the claim Session explicitly (execution-entry-service.ts:1920-1927). The test T deleted did not use the writer at all: seedLegacyActivity hand-wrote the legacy Run through commitRaw with no claim/outbox and then wrote the activity (before: tests/helpers/S2B-activity-fixture.ts:302-326, used by S2B-activity-calendar-tasks.test.ts:146-168). Only an old/hand-made Run reaches it; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Both proposals delete the compatibility count; the safe scope is Claude's: run-activity-service.ts:302 should refuse a missing dispatch as unavailable, RunActivitySnapshot.sessionRef becomes non-null (contracts/run-activity.ts:63; the codec is src/core/work-graph/persistence/run-activity-codecs.ts:288-293), then :345 and the null arm at :367 go. That edits the L9/L17 spec sentence (slice-2B-SPEC.md:430-436, :171) which still says old executions may be null, so the lead must sign the spec note; keeping it untested under rule 4 is the alternative.

U stands.

rows.evidence: Line 496 rejects a cell Session whose stored workspaceId differs from the bound workspace. The calendar is already bound to the Goal's workspace (activity-read-model.ts:234-239) and every cell Session comes from the claim/history SessionRef or a responsible link. Claims refuse a Session of another workspace (:997-998) and links do too: targetSession rejects a foreign Session (session-lifecycle.ts:203-213) and validateTaskTarget refuses a Goal of another workspace (session-targets.ts:87-93, reached from :149); link writers reuse the claim SessionRef. A Session's workspaceId is taken only from the creating scope (session-directory.ts:960-966, the field at :964) and later writes spread the stored record. The cross-workspace relation can only be made by cloning rows in the store, which is what T3-089 deleted (t-items-T3-w2.md:746-752). U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Both options are valid: codex's keep-untested matches rule 4, and Claude's delete of :486-502 is behaviour-equivalent for production data (the block's only job is the project check at :487 and workspace check at :496). Deleting is explicitly left to the lead by T3-089, removes one Session read per distinct Session (read-count literals in the cap tests change) and drops a scope guard for corrupt rows, so I recommend keeping it unless L17/R4 wants otherwise.

Also decide whether the frozen DTO is kept as an injection-only value.

rows.evidence: The anonymous callback at :413 runs only in the `architecture === null` branch (:412-414), i.e. when the current-catalog read is not_found (goal-conflicts.ts:365-380, :380). That pointer is ProjectArchitectureBaselineActive (catalog-service.ts:122-124, :368-373), the very record plan adoption requires: initial adoption is refused without resolved governance (plan-service.ts:1679-1682), which requires that pointer (plan-readers.ts:812-827). Executed files come from Runs, Runs require an accepted Plan (task-machine claim path), and no writer removes the pointer (only adopt/revise write it, catalog-service.ts:523-541, :701-720). So with architecture null the file list is necessarily empty and the callback can never be invoked; D2 stands. The test title 'no catalog adopted' is stale since TP-107 (tests/helpers/task-claim-fixture.ts:265-279 adopts a catalog).
rows.proposal_note: Replacing the null branch with [] and dropping the callback is behaviour-equivalent and nothing else calls it; cosmetic, so keeping it is also acceptable. No spec line reserves the null-with-files state.
